newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs agree to World Bank loan to boost oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs agree to World Bank loan to boost oilfield.

text.p: Kazakhstan's parliament has approved a $109 million plan by the World Bank to rehabilitate the giant Uzen oilfield, a parliamentary spokeswoman said on Friday.
"The loan now needs the president's (Nursultan Nazarbayev) approval, which we should get in the next few days," she said.

The World Bank proposal aims to boost output from the field, in southwest Kazakhstan 150 km east of the Caspian Sea, from 2.5 million tonnes a year (50,000 barrels per day) to 7.0-7.5 million tonnes (140,000 to 150,000 bpd).
Kazakh oil company AO Uzenmunaigaz, which holds a licence to the field, will contribute an additional $26 million.
Uzen is the focus of a high stakes international tender.
Kazakhstan has shortlisted Amoco Corp, Malaysia's Petronas and Chinese National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) and will announce a winner by November.

Uzen has estimated recoverable reserves of up to 150 million tonnes (about one billion barrels) and is Kazakhstan's second largest oilfield after Tengiz, which contains about one billion tonnes (over seven billion barrels).
